answer.rationale: Memory_73 explicitly warns that promotional pricing materially reduces 30-day retention despite acquisition lift—this directly contradicts the primary objective of sustainable long-term revenue, making it unsuitable as a panic response to competitive price pressure. Memory_57 demonstrates referral incentives work well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without retention harm. The competitor's attack targets price-sensitive SMB; referral incentives redirect retention energy toward expansion and customer acquisition without race-to-the-bottom pricing. This preserves unit economics and sustainable margins. While memory_31 and memory_91 show onboarding and activation messaging gains, those are architectural improvements orthogonal to immediate retention defense. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is valuable but slower to deploy at scale. Referral incentives activate your existing customer base as a retention and acquisition lever simultaneously, moving away from unsustainable price competition toward network effects. Standard experiment allows validation before broader rollout, acknowledging that established-customer success may not perfectly transfer to price-sensitive SMB under duress.
